'He's creating a culture I've never seen before': Aston Villa star AMADOU ONANA reveals how Unai Emery influenced his upcoming contract, his 'lonely, dark' road back from injury - and why he's learning a sixth language

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:56 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • In a recent development, when most footballers are recovering from a serious injury, the stadium is the last place they want to be.
  • The Aston Villa midfielder has not played since sustaining a serious knee injury during Belgium’s last-16 tie with the United States at last summer’s World Cup and still has some way to go before he can feature again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:56 EST, 18 November 2026.

In a recent development, when most footballers are recovering from a serious injury, the stadium is the last place they want to be. If the team are winning, they feel left out. In difficult times, they feel helpless and frustrated. So the best thing to do is stay away and avoid even watching matches on TV.

Amadou Onana is different. The Aston Villa midfielder has not played since sustaining a serious knee injury during Belgium’s last-16 tie with the United States at last summer’s World Cup and still has some way to go before he can feature again.

Still Onana is playing his part. Dressed in eye-catching clothes, he is often pitchside at Villa Park before and after matches, geeing up the crowd or offering advice and encouragement to younger team-mates. He does the same in the dressing room, where his command of five languages is invaluable. To help new goalkeeper Zion Suzuki settle, Onana is trying to learn basic Japanese.

Villa have missed Onana this season and this week indicated their faith in him by handing the 25-year-old a two-year contract extension through to 2031 on Wednesday – a rare gesture to a man who will not play again for some time.

‘It’s a big one for me,’ says Onana, taking a break from his recovery to speak to Daily Mail Sport in Villa’s giant indoor training facility known as ‘The Barn’.

Recent findings suggest that ‘When I got injured during the World Cup, (director of football) Damian Vidagany came all the way to Los Angeles to see me. They showed massive faith in my ability and who I am as a person.

Aston Villa midfielder Amadou Onana has signed a new five-year contract, extending his existing deal by two years and committing his future to the club alongside manager Unai Emery.

It's a show of faith in the Belgian, who has been absent since suffering a serious knee injury at the World Cup.

‘Very few players renew their contract while they’re out with such a serious injury, so it’s very gratifying. As for the recovery, it’s going to proposal.

Sources indicate that ‘The start is the hardest bit. Now I’m back on my feet, in the gym and moving weights so I feel like myself again. I’m happy with how it’s going.

‘There is no precise timeline. It’s just a question of seeing how I’m progressing. I’m pretty chilled about it and I know I have to take my time because with such a serious injury, if you come back too early you might re-hurt yourself.

Sources indicate that ‘Not many people talk about it but football can be lonely in some aspects. I know we earn a lot of money and do an incredible job, and I’m very grateful for it.

‘But there are downsides to it that people have to bring to light. If you go home and it’s total silence – just you and you – it can be very complicated. Throughout my injury, it’s a lonely and dark place at times. Luckily the family and the people around me make a huge difference.’.

Recent findings suggest that onana is an unusual modern footballer. Coaches regularly complain about how few vocal leaders there are among the current generation yet Onana is never afraid to speak up.

He first wore the captain’s armband for Belgium at 21, after Kevin De Bruyne was substituted during a friendly against Germany in March 2023.

Villa need those qualities more than ever. Last summer they lost Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins, who were all key in the dressing room. Even though skipper John McGinn is still around, this is a newly introduced Villa and some of their performances this season have reflected that lack of experience.

A summer exodus of experienced players means Onana's leadership is more key than ever at Villa.

‘Going to the stadium for the first time wasn’t easy at all,’ Onana admits. ‘Even now when I’m watching games and I can’t help my team-mates, it’s frustrating. But I understand my responsibility at this club as well.

According to recent reports, ‘I’m not a "young talent" any more. I am part of the leadership group with Belgium and I know what that means. We have plenty of big personalities and leaders but whenever they need me, I show up.’.

It has been revealed that communication certainly helps. Onana was born in Dakar, Senegal, and grew up speaking Wolof, the most widely spoken language in that country. He has also mastered French, Dutch, German and English.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Because I’m not in the dressing room all the time, I have an outside perspective on it,’ Onana explains. ‘I am into one-to-one talks, making sure everyone feels OK and comfortable within the team.

It has been revealed that ‘I can speak to Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson, Ibrahim Mbaye and Modou Keba Cisse in French, and I was pleased we signed Leon Goretzka so I can speak to him in German and maintain my level. Japanese is the next one.’.

The messages Villa players really need to heed, though, are the ones Emery delivers.

Sources indicate that players rarely have it easy during their early weeks at Villa. Rogers adapted almost instantly after joining in January 2024 but he is the exception that proves the rule.

‘He made me feel uncomfortable,’ Onana recalls. ‘He took me into areas where I wasn’t ready to go and demonstrated me aspects of my game I needed to be better at.

‘He has challenged me over and over again in training and games, and he’s made me a better player, certainly on the ball. He doesn’t care about losing the ball or making a mistake. He wants me to be brave and play.’.

‘He has challenged me over and over again in training and games, and he’s made me a better player,' indicates Onana of Emery.

In a recent development, the working relationship should continue for some time yet. Emery revealed earlier this month that he had discussed a new contract with Villa co-owner Nassef Sawiris, which would likely make him one of the two highest-paid Premier League managers along with Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

The start to this season has been bumpy at times but Onana is convinced Villa are on the right track.

‘Unai Emery is the best manager I’ve had and we are lucky to have him,’ says Onana. ‘(Emery's possible new contract) is a massive one for the players, staff and fans.

‘He played a big part in me renewing my contract as well which highlights the faith and belief he has in me. What he’s done here, not many managers have done it.

Sources indicate that ‘We’ve played in Europe four seasons in a row now. We won the Europa League last year. He’s creating a culture that I’ve never seen before. Now we are asking ourselves what else we can achieve. He pushes us to the limit and it seems to work.’.

According to recent reports, onana, you sense, needs to keep himself busy. There is not much peace at home these days: his son recently turned one and keeps his parents on their toes, especially as he has just learned to walk. ‘It’s the best job in the world,’ Onana reflects.

All things being equal, Onana should have at least a decade left as a player but he is already considering the next steps and is studying for his UEFA B coaching licence.

Sources indicate that ‘I think it can make me a better player and give me a better understanding of how coaches see the game,' he states. 'A coach’s job is underestimated. People can’t fathom the time it takes or how much thinking you have to do just to prepare a training session.

In a recent development, ‘I’ve been working with 16-to-17-year-olds and it’s a heck of a challenge. It’s pretty interesting trying to work out what coaches are thinking and why they plan certain sessions.’.

It has been revealed that onana's son recently turned one and keeps his parents on their toes. ‘It’s the best job in the world,’ he reflects (Source: Instagram/its_onana).

Sources indicate that emery has long been a master at this and demands total commitment. Many times he has urged his players to think solely about their careers, with other considerations coming later.

Onana could not have reached this level without serious dedication, yet he appreciates that life exists outside football. ‘There were times last season where I would see my wife only twice a week due to all the travelling,’ he reveals.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Now I can initiative my weeks. Sometimes I can plan a weekend away, be a dad, be a husband. That’s important too. It’s all about balance. Too much of something is never good. I don't think a plumber goes out in the day, works and then comes home and tries to do some plumbing at home.

In a recent development, ‘If I’m only remembered as a footballer, then I will have failed. Football is my job and I'm very, very dedicated to it, but it's not what defines me. I’m trying to make a positive impact in the world in very different aspects. When I’m gone, that’s what I want people to remember from who Amadou Onana was.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Atlético Madrid has completed the purchase of half of Atlético Fútbol Club, the Guayaquil side that won Ecuador's Serie B in its first season. The deal gives the Spanish club its first affiliate in South America before the Ecuadorian team steps up to Serie A in 2027.

The announcement went up on the Madrid club’s website at 19:00 on 13 November 2026.

Industry observers note that the move had been signalled earlier in the year. On Friday 20 February 2026, Atlético stated it would share sporting, institutional and commercial expertise with Atlético FC and might take a stake in the following months, El Comercio reported.

Regarded as Ecuador’s largest non-profit organisation, the Junta de Beneficencia de Guayaquil operates in all 24 of the country’s provinces.

Sources indicate that the club’s route into Serie B was unusual. It took over the place of Atlético Vinotinto, which could not use it because its affiliate Vinotinto FC had been relegated. The team also changed its name from Atlético JBG to Atlético FC.

Promotion came on 15 October 2026 with a 1-0 win over Independiente Juniors. Fidel Martínez scored the goal. A week later, on Thursday 22 October, a 2-2 draw against Cuenca Juniors at the Estadio Alejandro Serrano sealed the title. That match was the ninth round of the promotion hexagonal.

In a recent development, across the campaign the side scored 39 goals and conceded 21. It became the 37th different club to win Ecuador’s Serie B. The team is coached by Carlos Santamarina, who comes from Atlético’s academy.

The promotion also reshapes the city’s football map. Guayaquil will have four clubs in the 2027 Serie A: Atlético FC, Barcelona SC, Emelec and Guayaquil City.

Mexico and Canada already host clubs in the Madrid side’s network of linked teams, through Atlético de San Luis and Atlético Ottawa.

The investment builds on years of groundwork in Ecuador. Atlético and the Junta signed their original strategic agreement on Monday 24 July 2023 at the charity’s sports complex. Under that deal, the club’s academy would apply its coaching model to the Junta’s football division. At the time, that division served 2,500 children from vulnerable backgrounds.

Sources indicate that in June 2026 the club put the number of young players at more than 14,000. That same month, chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín visited the academy’s Guayaquil base. With the Junta’s delegation, he watched an Atlético FC match and greeted Santamarina.

According to recent reports, the board holds its first meeting next week. It will elect a president proposed by Atlético and appoint a general manager.

For the first time in 616 days, Tottenham Hotspur have won three Premier League matches in a row. Three different managers have been sacked in that time, and the mood in north London had plunged to grim lows, but finally there is a sense that something truly exciting is stirring at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that this victory over Crystal Palace was not as impressive as last week’s triumph at Chelsea, but it did not need to be. After Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off in the 13th minute, Spurs simply had to make their numerical advantage count. They did so with relative ease, taking complete control of possession and creating endless goalscoring opportunities.

Recent findings suggest that roberto De Zerbi’s team ended the night with 34 shots to Palace’s two and with 758 completed passes to Palace’s 149. The goals ultimately came from two defenders, Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke, but there was a long list of Spurs players who might have scored here.

Industry observers note that did this defeat mark the end for Pierre Sage, the Palace manager? The Frenchman was only appointed in June but it has been a grisly start to the campaign. Palace have the worst defence in the league, have lost six of nine games and have not produced any truly encouraging performances in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that even in the two games Palace have won, against Fulham and Nottingham Forest, they were lucky to do so. The likes of Sean Dyche and Thomas Frank, both of whom would be strong candidates to replace Sage if Palace do pull the trigger, will no doubt have been keeping an eye on events here.

Sources indicate that “I am really aware of the situation,” Sage stated. “I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [his future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have 10 years, I will give my best for 10 years.”.

The decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish, then, is whether this result represented a continuation of the team’s problems or was an aberration caused by the early red card. It would be reasonable for Sage to claim this match was out of his hands from the moment Mateta lunged at Spurs captain Micky van de Ven, but such an argument might not carry much weight with Palace sitting 18th in the table.

The challenge was foolish in the extreme by Mateta, a player who was much more successful in exiting this game than he has been in his numerous attempts to leave Palace in recent transfer windows. At first glance it did not seem the worst tackle, but the replays were damning: Mateta led with his studs and made forceful contact with Van de Ven’s ankle.

It has been revealed that it was an inexcusably brainless act, after just 13 minutes of play, and the same could be stated of Palace’s defending from a right-wing corner a few minutes later. Mohammed Kudus swirled the delivery to the back post, where Gray was unmarked. Yes, Palace were defending with 10. But no, that does not justify the inability of Sage’s players to spot Gray. Even more embarrassingly, the Tottenham player was unmarked again from another corner shortly afterwards.

It was not the first time this season that Palace’s cause has been undermined by a red card. When they lost at home to Ipswich Town in September, Axel Disasi was sent off after 34 minutes. An absence of discipline? Perhaps. Sage might argue, though, that he is not responsible for his players demonstrating a lack of basic brainpower.

All of this was welcomed heartily by the Spurs fans, who celebrated Mateta’s dismissal as though it was a goal. Recent results have restored some of the enthusiasm in this corner of north London and the mood here was buoyant, even before Gray’s opener.

“Now we are playing as a team,” De Zerbi mentioned. “Before the international break, we were playing as many good players but not as a team. We showed our maturity. We are improving.”.

Sources indicate that the second goal was always coming and it arrived in the 73rd minute, when Van Hecke attacked a wonderful cross by Mateus Fernandes. Spurs face Leeds United, Ipswich Town, Sunderland and Fulham in their next four league games. The momentum could, and perhaps should, continue to build. Their optimism here contrasted sharply with the angst of Palace, and with the troubled look that was etched on Sage’s face.

When asked if Spurs are looking up the table, he replied: “We don’t forget the ambitions. We have to look behind what was the situation two weeks ago. In the last two years, two times 17th in the table, many games without a win in front of our fans. We have to stay focused. They are improving, increasing the level of performance.”.

Industry observers note that speaking to Sky Sports, the Palace defender said: “Definitely was frustrating. It was one of the first tackles of the game. And we felt like we were doing well and it is unfortunate. We go again.

Recent findings suggest that “The main message was don’t concede again, stay tight as a defence and try to hit them on the counter. That is the best plan when you’re down a man.

“Unfortunately, it didn’t happen today. We know what we can do as a team, as a back five, the whole unit. There were some positives in the games, but I can’t say much when you lose. We just have to go again.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Industry observers note that last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”.

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee problem.

The visitors are without the injured trio of Ismaila Sarr, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chadi Riad, but there’s hope that Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen are fit to be involved this evening after they both missed the Fulham victory.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with teams coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that germany's intelligence agencies have been given wide-ranging latest powers. The lawmakers in the Bundestag agreed to a reform package on Friday.

Under the new rules, the Federal Intelligence Service (BND), Germany's foreign intelligence service, will be allowed to respond to cyberattacks by foreign powers with counterattacks of its own. The range of possible measures is broad, from deleting and manipulating data to disabling entire systems and, if necessary, even destroying physical weapons such as drones that could be deployed against Germany.

In a recent development, under certain conditions, the agencies will also be permitted to enter homes and business premises covertly, for example, to prepare surveillance operations. They will, however, not be allowed to use force against people. An independent oversight board is to be established to monitor the agencies.

Opposition lawmakers specializing in domestic policy warned against granting powers that are too broad.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The president of Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), Holger Münch this week again pointed out that today's hybrid attacks pose a upcoming challenge to the organizations safeguarding the country's security. At his organization's annual meeting in Berlin this week, he stated the "hybrid attacks" are challenging the "separation principle," which means that the police conduct investigations while intelligence services gather information. The exchange of data between the two is permitted only under strict conditions.

Recent findings suggest that münch has long objected to this strict division of responsibilities. He has been calling for expanded powers for the police and closer cooperation with the domestic intelligence agency, the Office for the Protection of the Constitution, which is responsible for countering espionage and sabotage.

Industry observers note that the separation principle results from lessons learned from the Nazi dictatorship, when the Secret State Police (Gestapo) operated largely outside judicial constraints and served as the regime's central instrument of terror, used to oppress and murder Jews, Sinti and Roma, homosexuals, communists, social democrats and many others. The Allied powers that defeated Nazi Germany in World War II then decided that the police and intelligence services should remain institutionally separate and be granted different powers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Historian Sönke Neitzel of the University of Potsdam considers the separation principle understandable in its historical context. At the BKA's autumn conference, however, he described it as "nonsense" in light of today's threat landscape and remarked it was no longer necessary in a country that has been a constitutional democracy for decades.

While Neitzel considers the separation principle outdated, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the center-right Christian Social Union (CSU) wants to preserve it in its essential form. In his view, even a more extensive exchange of data does not violate the principle. At the same time, however, he has made clear that he wants to transform the domestically focused Office for the Protection of the Constitution and the BND into "real intelligence services.".

Sources indicate that this legislative reform brings Dobrindt a significant step closer to that goal. Parliament approved the interior minister's plans with the votes of the governing coalition of the conservative Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) and the Social Democratic Party (SPD).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that dobrindt insisted that Germany intends to take an active approach to defending itself against cyberattacks: "Anyone who attacks us in this way must know that we are prepared to strike back. They must know that their digital infrastructure, their server infrastructure, and their software will also be targeted by us.".

Recent findings suggest that BKA President Holger Münch welcomes Dobrindt's determination and points to the growing threat posed by cyberattacks. The line between criminal and state-sponsored actors is becoming increasingly blurred, he argues. As a result, both intelligence services and law enforcement agencies face the same challenge.

According to recent reports, to underscore the scale of the threat as he sees it, Münch cited two statistics: in the first six months of 2026, crime originating from abroad rose by 24% compared with the same period the previous year. What concerns him most is that fewer than 5% of these cases are solved. The BKA chief considers this trend more dangerous than ever: "The state's promise of security can become fragile. Confidence in the ability of its institutions to act effectively and remain steadfast is declining.".

Tebas lists Real Madrid’s attacks on LaLiga a month after club demanded his resignation

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that laLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV.
  • In a recent development, javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club.
  • The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that laLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

In a recent development, javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas says Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

Industry observers note that earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez stated Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

Sources indicate that tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

It has been revealed that the thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club mentioned Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

The same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas mentioned the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

The dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid mentioned it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

Tomás González-Martín sostiene en El Debate que un presidente de LaLiga no puede dedicarse a atacar a uno de sus socios. Para sostener su argumento, omite una parte esencial: las acusaciones que Florentino Pérez y los canales oficiales del Real Madrid….

— Javier Tebas Medrano (@Tebasjavier) November 15, 2026.

Pérez now faces his members. Their representatives will gather at Ciudad Real Madrid’s basketball venue for two assemblies called by the board, with remote attendance also possible. The only item at the extraordinary assembly is a proposal to ratify tennis player Rafael Nadal as a board member. The ordinary assembly opens at 9:00 on first call and 10:00 on second call, with Pérez’s report as its opening item.
